# PetTranslator.ai

> Premium AI-powered behavioral analysis for dog and cat owners. Upload one photo, get a vet-behaviorist-style report — observed body-language markers, the behavioral state they suggest, an owner action plan you can apply today. AVSAB-aligned, force-free training only, no dominance theory.

## What this site is

PetTranslator.ai is a web-first multimodal AI service. The marketing site (pettranslator.ai) is a static editorial publication; the app (app.pettranslator.ai) is where the AI inference runs. The site exists to communicate methodology, publish behaviorist-grade guides, and convert qualified visitors into Free trial users.

## What this site is not

- Not a cartoon "pet translator" app that invents fake dialogue ("Mommy, I love you!").
- Not a bark-to-English translator. Dogs don't operate at human sentence-level cognition.
- Not a veterinary diagnostic tool. We document visible behavioral markers; we don't diagnose disease.
- Not a training program. We point users toward force-free, evidence-based methods and AVSAB-credentialed professionals when relevant.

## Pricing

- **Free**: 3 behavioral analyses, lifetime (not daily, not monthly). No signup required for the first three.
- **Premium**: $4.99/month or $39.99/year (33% discount). 30 analyses/month, up to 5 pet profiles, vet-ready PDF exports, behavioral trends across uploads.
- Refund: 7-day full refund window on first charge. Cancel anytime, one click.
- Privacy: Anthropic enterprise API terms apply. Uploads are never used to train AI models.

## Methodology

The AI is Claude Sonnet 4.6 (multimodal). The system prompt (v1.2.1) constrains output to:

1. **Observed markers** — physical signals visible in the photo (ear angle, tail carriage, pupil dilation, posture, lip line, weight distribution). The model documents what it sees before interpreting.
2. **Behavioral interpretation** — a third-person clinical reading of what those markers typically indicate, with confidence calibration.
3. **Owner action plan** — concrete Do / Avoid behaviors aligned with AVSAB position statements on humane training. No correction-based methods recommended, ever.
4. **Confidence + uncertainty disclosure** — every report states what the model is confident about and what it isn't.

We follow AVSAB position statements on humane dog training (2021), positive-reinforcement training (2007), the use of dominance theory in animal behavior modification (2007), and force-free veterinary care.

## Content

The blog (60+ articles, ~150K words) is a behaviorist's reference covering:

- Dog body language (ears, eyes, tail, posture, jaw tension, vocalization)
- Cat body language (ear angle, slow blinking, tail position, ground-level signals)
- "What does it mean when..." high-intent searches
- Stress, anxiety, fear — escalation ladders and intervention timing
- Force-free training fundamentals (recall, loose-leash, crate, carrier training)
- Breed-specific behavior patterns
- Senior pet behavioral changes and cognitive decline
- Why dominance theory is wrong (anti-pattern guidance)

All articles use third-person clinical voice, cite primary research, and link to professional resources (AVSAB, IAABC, certified veterinary behaviorists).
